notation.C_H: hub's incidence-forest component -- Claude-branch-only notation, not found in the Codex research corpus
notation.C_R1: the incidence-forest component containing vertex (q, R1_target_orbit)
notation.D: sum of unused phases per open orbit (computed property)
notation.E_orbit: orbit of a permutation word under right-multiplication by E=sigma^(n-1)*tau; 144 orbits in S6
notation.F: abandonment counter (F_def, TARGET_F=1 for the whole RR program)
notation.P: sum of used orbit phases (computed property)
notation.Phi_name_collision: Phi is used for two different things in this project: (1) the project-wide monotone capacity potential Phi(S)=5+6*(TARGET_P-S.P)-(720-S.visited_count); (2) an informal Claude-branch-only notation Phi(q) meaning the fixed phase-to-hexagon incidence set of orbit q, used only in the VNTS lemma discussion
notation.R1_R2: first and second R events in an RR word
notation.R_event: weight-3 non-abandoning joint with new_orbit=False (re-entry into an already-open orbit)
notation.Target_A: an R2 macro-edge whose child has F_def=1,H=0 and whose R2 source/target orbits share an incidence component
notation.Target_B: an admissible R-free, F/H-preserving terminal continuation from a Target-A boundary
notation.VNTS: Visited Non-Terminal Source lemma, introduced in research/RR_SHORT_T4_GENERIC_THEORY_CLAUDE.md
notation.Z2: the engine's unique weight-2 non-abandoning move
notation.Z3: weight-3 non-abandoning joint with new_orbit=True (opens a fresh orbit)
notation.bridge: the mechanism merging the R1-orbit's incidence component with another (e.g. the hub's) via a shared hexagon vertex
notation.component_changing_Z3: a Z3 edge whose target hexagon is already in an existing incidence-forest component
notation.hexagon: orbit of a word under rotation sigma alone; 120 hexagons in S6
notation.hub: in an F<=1 word, the unique hexagon (if any) that is the target of >=2 distinct joints over the whole word

engine_universal_assumptions: unique weight-2 move, bijective action -> unique predecessor per target
vnts_lemma.full_hex_corollary: if an entire hexagon is full and no anchor's endpoint lies in it, VNTS applies to all six windows simultaneously
vnts_lemma.name: Visited Non-Terminal Source (VNTS)
per_anchor_assumptions: H1: sigma visited at every anchor
H2: no anchor terminal at sigma
vnts_lemma.statement: Let tau be a literal window targeted by the engine's unique weight-2 move, sigma its unique weight-2 predecessor, A a finite anchor family. If (H1) sigma visited at every anchor and (H2) no anchor's endpoint equals sigma, then no exact descendant of A can ever be at sigma, so the move into tau can never fire in any descendant.
vnts_lemma.unresolved_generalization: hub-hexagon-set engine-universality is explicitly left open; no branch other than short_ell2_r1_37 has attempted the 7-item certificate checklist
vnts_lemma.why_h82_not_a_fullness_obstruction: VNTS never requires the target's own hexagon to be full, only that some hexagon (wherever the predecessor lives) is full-and-non-terminal
